title: Fourier coefficient bound for a twisted lift of an $\varepsilon$-far function
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $n \ge 0$, and write $\omega_p = e^{2\pi i/p}$ for the primitive $p$-th root of unity. Let $f : \bbz_p^{\,n} \to \bbz_p$ be normalized ($f(0)=0$) and $\varepsilon$-far from linear, meaning $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$ and $\Pr_x[f(x)\ne g(x)] \ge \varepsilon$ for every additive homomorphism $g : \bbz_p^{\,n} \to \bbz_p$. Fix $j \in \bbz_p$ with $j \ne 0$, and for $s \in \bbz_p^{\,n}$ let $\widehat{h}(s) = \E_x\bigl[h(x)\,\omega_p^{-\,s\cdot x}\bigr]$ denote the Fourier coefficient of a function $h : \bbz_p^{\,n} \to \bbc$ at frequency $s$, where $s\cdot x = \sum_{i} s_i x_i \in \bbz_p$. Then the $j$-twisted lift $\widetilde{f}_j(x) = \omega_p^{\,j\,f(x)}$ satisfies
\[
  \operatorname{Re}\,\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s) \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\,\varepsilon
\]
for every $s \in \bbz_p^{\,n}$.
replaced:
If $f : \mathbb{Z}_p^n \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ is $\varepsilon$-far from linear
(normalized), $j \ne 0$, and $s \in \mathbb{Z}_p^n$, then
\[
  \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\widehat{(\widetilde{f}_j)}(s)\right]
  \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1-\cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\varepsilon.
\]
